Class CharneyVegetationAlbedoEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.engine.AbstractSimulationEngine
org.ether.society.engines.tier1.CharneyVegetationAlbedoEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
SimulationEngineModule
public class CharneyVegetationAlbedoEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine
Charney Vegetation-Albedo Dynamic Bistability & Abrupt Desertification Engine.

Models the coupled non-linear feedback between surface albedo, monsoonal precipitation, and vegetation cover across the Saharo-Sahelian belt, based on the canonical models of Jule Charney (1975), Victor Brovkin et al. (1998), and Martin Claussen et al. (1999):

Charney Radiative Subsidence Mechanism: High surface albedo of bare desert sand ($\alpha_{\text{sand}} \approx 0.38$) enhances net radiative cooling of the tropospheric column, driving atmospheric subsidence (sinking motion), suppressing convective precipitation, and maintaining hyper-aridity. Conversely, dense vegetation cover ($V \in [0, 1]$, $\alpha_{\text{veg}} \approx 0.16$) absorbs solar radiation, fueling thermal convection and monsoonal rainfall: $$\alpha(V) = \alpha_{\text{sand}} (1 - V) + \alpha_{\text{veg}} V$$ $$P = \max\left(20.0, P_{\text{base}} + \Delta P_{\text{orbital}}(\varpi) + \gamma_{\text{albedo}} (\alpha_{\text{crit}} - \alpha)\right)$$

Cusp Catastrophe & Mid-Holocene Green Sahara Collapse (~-4,100 BCE): The equilibrium vegetation cover obeys the analytical saturation formulation: $$V^*(P) = 1.0 - \exp\left(-\frac{\max(0.0, P - P_{\text{crit}})}{P_{\text{scale}}}\right)$$ Driven by the Milankovitch precession cycle ($\varpi$, 23 ka), as orbital insolation declines past the critical saddle-node bifurcation threshold around $-4\,100$ BCE (6,000 BP), the system undergoes an abrupt transition from the "Green Sahara" state ($V > 0.60$) to the modern hyper-arid desert ($V invalid input: '<' 0.05$) within ~200-300 years, catalyzing the pastoralist migration into the Nile Valley and the genesis of the Egyptian Old Kingdom.

  • Method Details

    • calculateOrbitalMonsoonAnomalyMm

      public static double calculateOrbitalMonsoonAnomalyMm(double currentYear)
      Calculates the Milankovitch precession orbital monsoon rainfall anomaly in mm/year. During the Holocene Thermal Maximum (~9,000 to ~6,000 BP), precession placed perihelion in boreal summer, strengthening the African monsoon by up to ~180 mm/year (Kutzbach 1981; deMenocal et al. 2000; Claussen et al. 1999).
      Parameters:
      currentYear - simulation year (negative for BCE/BP)
      Returns:
      orbital rainfall perturbation in mm/year
